idiom_name: bounded queue + one explicit full-policy + drop instrumentation
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: declare the capacity as data next to the queue's construction, pick exactly one full-behaviour - block/await, fail the producer (exception, false return or error value), drop oldest, drop newest, coalesce, or spill to durable storage - and make that behaviour visible at the call site instead of implicit in which send method was used. Admission and mutation must be one atomic step so two producers cannot both see room for the last slot. Count and tag every shed or rejected item so the loss has an owner and can be attributed, and size the capacity from a throughput/latency budget rather than from the heap: the buffer exists to absorb transients, not to convert sustained overload into queueing delay.
code_sketch:
buffer = BoundedQueue(capacity = 10_000, policy = DROP_OLDEST)

if not buffer.try_push(msg):        # the decided outcome, visible at one place
    drops.increment(tags = {queue: buffer.name, reason: "full"})
    diverts.put(msg)                # optional durable overflow path
# consumer: msg = buffer.pop()  - blocking policy would await here instead
pitfalls: Deriving the policy from the send method used (put vs offer vs add) rather than choosing it: the call site then documents nothing and the failure mode is an accident.
Checking free capacity and pushing in two steps: two producers admit the same last slot, and the bound is violated exactly under the load it was meant to survive.
Choosing block in a path that also holds a lock or runs on a single event-loop thread: the producer stalls the very thread that would drain the buffer.
